answer: Each identity runs one harbor gate and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a ledger: quartz gauge inflow at its quartz sensor and bridge channel outflow at its bridge span, in the atlas ledger. A harbor auditor recomputes inflow minus outflow from atlas records; a mismatch or reused reading burns the bond. Fees rise: gate k costs 28+6(k-1); gate 1000 costs 6022, so 1000 fakes cost 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails: a rented reading carries its owner's key, and its gauge is claimed. An honest keeper pays 28 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
